summary: Ripe plantain slices fried until caramelised, with crisp golden edges and a soft, sweet centre.
story: Dodo is a Yoruba name for fried ripe plantain, and it is eaten across Nigeria beside jollof rice, beans, stews and many other meals. It is also sold as a snack and sometimes sprinkled with a little salt or chilli.

steps.title: Peel and slice
steps.text: Peel the plantains. Slice on a diagonal into pieces about 1 cm thick for oval shapes. Keep them an even thickness so they cook uniformly.

steps.title: Salt lightly
steps.text: Toss the slices with a small pinch of salt, which balances the sweetness. Do not add too much.

steps.title: Heat the oil
steps.text: Pour oil into a wide frying pan to a depth of about 1.5 cm and heat over medium heat. A slice dropped in should sizzle gently and not spit aggressively.

steps.title: Fry first side
steps.text: Add as many slices as fit without touching. Fry for 2 to 3 minutes until the underside is deep golden brown, with darker caramelised edges.

steps.title: Flip and finish
steps.text: Turn each slice and fry another 2 minutes until golden on both sides. Very ripe plantains brown quickly, so lower the heat if they darken too fast.

steps.title: Drain
steps.text: Lift out onto paper towels. Serve while hot, as dodo softens as it cools.

tips: Plantain must be very ripe, almost black, for sweet dodo. Yellow ones turn starchy.
Do not crowd the pan or the plantains steam rather than fry.
Medium heat is best: too hot and the sugar burns before the middle softens.
For less oil, brush with oil and bake at 220°C.

swaps.swap: Very ripe, firm bananas can stand in, though they are softer and sweeter and cook in about half the time.
Groundnut or sunflower oil both work.

name: Dodo (Fried Plantain)
